title: Prescriptions Compliance Manual: Short Fills and Owed Balances
content:
When Kestrel dispenses a fill of Kestrel Prescriptions short of the prescribed quantity, the units still owed are booked on the prescription's fill ledger as an owed-balance entry, and that owed balance stays open until a balance completion or a balance cancellation names it.

## Section 1 — When a fill may go short

A fill is dispensed short only where the class allows a short fill and the number of owed balances open on the prescription is below the class's limit on open owed balances. The shortfall is booked as an owed balance at no additional charge, the fill's patient pay already covering the full prescribed quantity.

An owed balance is **open** when its owed-balance entry is named by no balance completion entry and no balance cancellation entry on the fill ledger; the count looks at the whole history of the prescription.

## Section 2 — Completion window

- For a Schedule II Controlled Prescription, the balance is completed no later than the date the prescriber wrote the prescription plus the partial-fill completion days.
- For every other class, the balance is completed no later than the date the fill was dispensed short plus the partial-fill completion days.
- Days are calendar days with the anchor date as day 0. The anchor of each class is the date its completion-anchor setting names. The last day of the window itself qualifies. The dates come from the prescription record and the fill ledger.

## Section 3 — Settling an owed balance

- A balance completion dispenses exactly the owed units of the one owed-balance record it names and never more; each owed balance is settled once, by one completion or one cancellation.
- An owed balance not completed by its last day, or declined by the patient, is cancelled for its full owed units.
- A cancelled Schedule II balance is void and needs a new prescription; for every other class the cancelled units are not re-dispensed and the next fill follows the ordinary refill rules.

## Windows worked through (hypothetical dates)

| Class and window | Anchor | Completion on the last day | Completion one day later |
|---|---|---|---|
| Schedule II, 30 days | written on day 0, short fill on day 4 | day 30 qualifies | day 31 does not; the balance is cancelled |
| Other class, 14 days | short fill on day 0 | day 14 qualifies | day 15 does not; the balance is cancelled |

## Questions answered

**The patient no longer wants the owed units.** A balance the patient declines is cancelled for its full owed units.

**Can a completion hand out more than was owed?** No. It dispenses exactly the owed units of the owed-balance record it names.

**With one owed balance open and a class limit of 1, may another fill go short?** No; the count of open owed balances must be below the limit.
